text: Daily gather: 4 products / 26 new ingredients, all four from manufacturer disclosures read this run. Arm & Hammer Liquid Laundry Detergent - Baking Soda Fresh and Xtra Liquid Laundry Detergent - Tropical Passion (both Church & Dwight product ingredient disclosure forms, materials 42019452 and 42015436); Glass Plus Cleaner and Lime-A-Way Toilet Bowl Cleaner (both Reckitt SmartLabel, productLineId 316 and 320). Laundry was the gap: the DB carried Arm & Hammer's washing soda and OxiClean but not the brand's mainstream liquid detergent, and carried no Xtra at all. Grading follows the house >=40% ECHA C&L consensus rule read from PubChem PUG View; UVCB/polymer substances with no discrete CID (orange terpenes, hydrogenated rosin, acrylic acid homopolymer, C12-13 alcohols ethoxylated, PEG-2 hydrogenated tallow amine) are recorded Extrapolated with a class analogy, never graded. Fragrance components are listed individually where the disclosure lists them individually (Church & Dwight publishes them at or above 100 ppm or on a designated list). Two named findings: (1) Nitrilotriacetic acid, disclosed by Church & Dwight as a non-functional constituent of Arm & Hammer liquid detergent, is flagged CA Prop 65 on the disclosure itself and grades canc C (H351 67%); (2) Galaxolide (hexamethylindanopyran), a polycyclic musk in both Arm & Hammer and Xtra, grades env F on a 97.9% H400 consensus and is flagged US EPA PBTs on the disclosure, with non-consensus H360/H361 reproductive codes recorded but not graded. Also fixed a live validator failure: the Methanol record carried 'organ' in impacts[], which is a valid grade dimension but not a valid impact tag, so chem_maintain.py had been reporting an issue; the organ damage is already carried by gr.organ=F. Counts: 193 -> 197 products, 304 -> 330 ingredients. dedupe guard: no duplicates.

Spectrum build station 2 (Dolman): exposure-ordered harvest of the thin tiers, 11 products, 24 new ingredients graded from PubChem PUG REST GHS, 5 owner records added. Drugstore tier 2->4, dollar-store 2->3, grocery 8->15, apothecary-bulk 10->11. Every ingredient list copied from a manufacturer or government disclosure read that night: Whole Foods household-cleaner disclosure (CA SB-258), Sprouts CA Cleaning Product Right to Know declarations, DailyMed (NLM) FDA OTC drug labels for CVS Health, Walgreens and Power Force, the La Corona SDS plus retailer panel for Zote, and the Kirk's manufacturer ingredient page. Corrected ownership: Whole Foods Market, 365 Everyday Value and 365 by Whole Foods Market now resolve to Amazon.com, Inc. (verified, June 2017 merger announcement) instead of sitting in no-parent-found. Dollar Tree's record now carries the Power Force house brand and names Korex Chicago LLC as its labeler of record. Products carry tier, tier_src, exposure, exposure_src, owner and substitutes; none carries an as-sold grade, because grading them is the Sifter lane's job and a blank is honest. Dollar-store finding extended: the tier built for buyers with the least information still discloses the least, and the one public label in it is public only because it is an FDA drug label.

Sifter lane (verify): spot-checked 6 graded ingredients against PubChem PUG REST GHS — Citric Acid (H319 84.7%), Sodium Carbonate (H319), Methylisothiazolinone (H317 + stronger acute-tox codes H301/H311/H314/H318 noted), Limonene (H226/H304/H315/H317/H400), Caprylyl Glucoside (H315/H319/H335 at 50%), Feldspar (H373 100%) — all consistent with repo records. CORRECTED Benzotriazole: previous g-string H302,H315,H319,H410 overstated; PubChem CID 7220 ECHA C&L consensus supports only H302 (96.7%) and H319 (87.8%) above the 40% threshold; H315/H410 not supported; env D grade withdrawn and gr_ruled:[env] added per docs/decisions.md 2026-09-23 rule; H332 (37.7%) sub-threshold noted. Gather: 4 popular US cleaning products with public disclosures - Liquid-Plumr Pro-Strength Clog Destroyer Gel with Pipeguard (Clorox SDS US001283, issued 28-May-2021), Ajax Dishwashing Liquid Lemon (Colgate-Palmolive SDS 660000000049, rev. 2016-03-21), Folex Instant Carpet Spot Remover (Folex California Ingredient Disclosure), and Old English Lemon Oil Furniture Polish (Reckitt SDS via rbnainfo.com). 7 new ingredients. 1 graded from PubChem/ECHA C&L via tools/ghs_lookup.py with the notifier consensus cited and every sub-40% code named: TEA Dodecylbenzene Sulfonate (CID 33782, title 'dodecylbenzenesulfonic acid, triethanolamine salt' - matches: H315 87.1% and H319 55.2% -> derm D; H301 15.2%, H302 20.6%, H318 26.3% below threshold, not graded). 1 recorded Not Classified on a stated consensus: Benzenesulfonic acid, C10-16-alkyl derivs., magnesium salts (UVCB CAS 68584-26-9; looked up by the class analog 'Magnesium dodecyl benzene sulfonate', CID 168704, title matches the class - H302, H315 and H319 each at 16.7%, all below the house >=40% threshold, so no dimension grade is justified). 5 recorded unclassified/extrapolated with explicit sourcing notes because they are UVCB/polymers/generic class descriptors with no PubChem CID (C12-14 Alcohol EO 3:1 Sodium Sulfate, Acrylic Polymer, Primary Amine, Distillates (petroleum), hydrotreated middle, Compound Based on Anionic and Nonionic Surfactants) - never an invented grade. Every PubChem title was checked against the intended substance before accepting the record. Three findings worth naming: (1) Old English Lemon Oil Furniture Polish contains no citrus oil in its disclosed composition - the current SDS lists a single component, a hydrotreated middle petroleum distillate at >60%, and states nothing else is classified as hazardous; an earlier SDS for the same line listed white mineral oil at 90-100% instead, so the carrier has changed across reformulations. (2) Liquid-Plumr is a two-active product (sodium hypochlorite 5-10%, sodium hydroxide 1-5%) whose hazard is the combination - the SDS warns explicitly against use with ammonia, toilet-bowl cleaners or any other drain opener because of hazardous gas release. (3) Ajax classifies the finished product as 'Not a hazardous substance or mixture' while its own SDS records that the LAS component causes severe skin irritation and eye irritation reversing within 21 days - the finished-product call rests on dilution, not on the ingredients being mild. This run also CLOSED the last 3 unknown-ingredient validation errors inherited from the spectrum lane, which had left chem_maintain.py exiting 1 on main for two days. The three were spelling variants of keys already in the database, not data gaps, so the product references were repointed at the canonical keys rather than minting duplicate entries: 'Sodium C10-16 Alkylbenzenesulfonate' -> Sodium (C10-16) Alkylbenzenesulfonate, 'Sodium Xylene Sulfonate' -> Sodium Xylenesulfonate, 'Orange Oil Blend' -> Orange Oil. Each repointed product carries a disclosure_note recording the source spelling. The fourth error, PowerHouse's 'Compound Based on Anionic and Nonionic Surfactants', is a genuine gap - a class descriptor rather than a chemical name - and was added as an extrapolated record with the class-level disclosure named as the finding. Dedupe guard: no duplicates. chem_maintain.py and tools/validate_certainty.py both pass. 182 products, 280 ingredients.

Gather: 4 popular US cleaning products with public disclosures - all free clear Original Concentrated Liquid Laundry Detergent (Henkel CAS-numbered disclosure), Comet with Bleach Cleanser (KIK California Cleaning Product Right to Know disclosure 12/6/2019), Lysol Laundry Sanitizer Free & Clear (Reckitt SmartLabel productLineId 2504), and Microban 24 Hour Multi-Purpose Cleaner and Disinfectant Spray Fresh Scent (P&G SmartLabel UPC 00037000485896, updated 2024-04-18). 8 new ingredients. 2 graded from PubChem/ECHA C&L via tools/ghs_lookup.py with the notifier consensus percentages cited and every sub-40% code named: Didecyldimethylammonium Chloride (CID 23558, title verified: H314 100% -> derm F, H302 85.8% -> work D, H400 47.6% -> env F; H318 28.4%, H410 22.4%, H411 34.7% below threshold, not graded) and Dioctyldimethylammonium Chloride (CID 62581, title verified: H314 99.6% -> derm F, H400 90.1% -> env F, H301 62.8% and H310 62.4% -> work F). 1 recorded Not Classified on a stated consensus: Octyl Decyl Dimethyl Ammonium Chloride (CID 61906, title 'Decyl dimethyl octyl ammonium chloride' - matches; H302/H314/H400 all at 31.4%, below the house >=40% threshold, so no dimension grade is justified). 5 recorded unclassified/extrapolated with explicit sourcing notes because they are UVCB/polymers/generic names with no PubChem CID (Alkyl C12-16 Dimethylbenzyl Ammonium Chloride, C12-15 Alcohols Ethoxylated, Alkylbenzene Sulfonic Acid, Polyethyloxazoline, Sodium Phosphate) - never an invented grade. Every PubChem title was checked against the intended substance before accepting the record. Three findings worth naming: (1) Comet with Bleach is bleached by trichloroisocyanuric acid, a chlorinated isocyanurate, not sodium hypochlorite - 'with bleach' in a US scouring powder does not mean chlorine bleach, and a Canadian SDS for the same line warns that long-term dust overexposure may produce evidence of dust in the lungs. (2) Lysol Laundry Sanitizer Free & Clear is fragrance-free but its actives are the same four quaternary ammonium compounds as the scented versions, three of them on California's Priority Chemicals list and two carrying an AOEC asthmagen designation; quats are designed to remain on the fabric after the rinse, which is the point of the product and also the exposure. (3) all free clear is the leading sensitive-skin detergent and EPA Safer Choice certified, and its CAS-numbered disclosure shows what 'free and clear' does and does not mean - no fragrance and no dye, but still an alcohol-ethoxylate surfactant, sodium laureth sulfate and benzisothiazolinone (a potent contact allergen and aquatic toxicant); EPA states it did not independently analyse the formula. This run also closed 5 of the 8 unknown-ingredient validation errors inherited from tools/apply_spectrum.py, because the four quat actives the Great Value products reference are now real ingredient records. The remaining 3 are naming variants of existing keys and are a lane-owner decision, not a data gap: 'Sodium C10-16 Alkylbenzenesulfonate' vs the existing 'Sodium (C10-16) Alkylbenzenesulfonate', 'Sodium Xylene Sulfonate' vs 'Sodium Xylenesulfonate', and 'Orange Oil Blend' vs 'Orange Oil'. Each new product record carries its source and source_url. 169 products, 272 ingredients.

Removed the DIY mixing lab. This database grades the products I bring into your home, it does not teach you to mix your own. Knowing what actually cleans, what is safe around your kids and dogs, and what should never touch your stone counters is the job I do. Every product entry stays. The mixing tool is gone.

Gather: 4 popular US cleaning products with public disclosures - Tide PODS Laundry Detergent Pacs Original Scent (P&G SmartLabel, updated 2026-02-19), Dawn Powerwash Dish Spray Fresh (P&G SmartLabel, updated 2024-12-18), Lysol Disinfecting Wipes Crisp Linen (Reckitt SmartLabel), and Clorox Toilet Bowl Cleaner with Bleach Fresh Scent (Clorox SmartLabel, updated 4/14/2025). 27 new ingredients. 11 graded from PubChem/ECHA C&L via tools/ghs_lookup.py with the notifier consensus percentages cited and every sub-40% code named: Sodium Bisulfite H302 99.9% (H334/H372 listed without percentages - sulfite asthma trigger, noted not graded); Denatonium Benzoate H302 95.1%, H332 83.4%, H412 83.2% (the bittering agent added to stop children swallowing pods is itself harmful if swallowed); Methyl Di-t-butyl Hydroxyhydrocinnamate H411 99.7% (H361 repro listed without a percentage - noted not graded); Citronellol H317 99.6%, H315 95.7%, H319 65.1%; Sodium Xylenesulfonate H319 66.8%; Sodium Laurate H318 67.4%, H315 71.8%, H335 45.6%; Sodium Caprate H412 94.7%; Sodium Caprylate H314 46.6%, H318 46.6%; Potassium Iodide H372 43.6% (H360/H362 listed without percentages - noted not graded); 4-tert-Butylcyclohexyl Acetate H317 80.3%, H411 82.4%; Floral Pyranol H319 >99.9%. 16 recorded unclassified or extrapolated with explicit sourcing notes because they are UVCB/polymers/soap salts with no PubChem CID (MEA C10-16 Alkylbenzenesulfonate, MEA Laureth Sulfate, MEA Salts of C12-18 Fatty Acids, MEA-citrate, PEG-136 Polyvinyl Alcohol, Hydrogenated Castor Oil, Styrene/Acrylates Copolymer, Zeolite, Dipropylene Glycol Butyl Ether, C9-11 Alkyl Glucoside, Sodium Myristate, Sodium Palmitate, Sodium Stearate, Pigment Green 7, Benzyl Dimethyl Carbinyl Acetate, Tetrahydromyrcenol) - never invented. Every PubChem title was checked against the intended substance before accepting the record: 'Quartz' returned CID 24261 titled 'Silica' (amorphous, not crystalline quartz) and was discarded; 'Sodium Caprylate' returned 'Sodium octanoate' and 'Floral Pyranol' returned 'Tetrahydro-4-methyl-2-(2-methylpropyl)-2H-pyran-4-ol' - both correct synonyms, kept and noted. 1 regulatory entry added: Citronellol (EU Annex III declarable fragrance allergen vs the US, where only the word 'fragrance' is required). Disclosure gaps found and NOT papered over: (1) The Pink Stuff Miracle Cleaning Paste is one of the most popular cleaning products in the US but has no usable ingredient disclosure - the manufacturer Star Brands SDS lists only the reportable components (Quartz 30-60%, Sodium Palmate 1-5%, Sodium Cocoate 1-5%, Glycerine <1%) and a regional distributor page lists a different set entirely (Soap, Sodium Silicate, Sodium Bicarbonate, Glycerin, Parfum, Laurylamine). No product record was created because the ingredient list cannot be stated honestly; this is a transparency finding, not a data gap. (2) 'Fragrance Ingredient' on the Clorox label is a catch-all already covered by the existing 'Fragrance' entry, and 'Alcohol Denat.' was mapped to the existing 'Ethanol' entry rather than creating a near-duplicate key. Each new product record carries its source and source_url field. Validation: data checks passed, 0 duplicates, index rebuilt.

Gather: 4 popular US cleaning products with public disclosures - Goo Gone Original adhesive remover (manufacturer SDS rev. 9/19/2024 + ingredient disclosure PDF), Shout Advanced Stain Remover Action Gel (SC Johnson SmartLabel + SDS 350000035250), The Works Toilet Bowl Cleaner (CA Cleaning Products Right to Know disclosure 12/27/2019 + manufacturer SDS + EPA label 5185-505-80306), and Bounce Fabric Softener Sheets Outdoor Fresh (P&G SmartLabel). 17 new ingredients. Grading: 4 graded from PubChem/ECHA C&L with consensus denominators cited - Orange Oil (CID 62161, dominant block 10 notifications/262 reports: H315 90.5%, H317 90.5% -> derm D + allerg, H318 44.7% -> derm D, H411 90.1% -> env D; H226 at 39.7% below threshold, not graded); Methenamine (CID 4101, dominant block 19 notifications/1051 reports: H317 100% -> derm C + allerg); Undeceth-3 (CID 61930, two single-company notifications: H318 100% -> derm D, flagged Low confidence); Nonoxynol (CID 24773, 2 notifications/3 reports: H315 100% -> derm C, H412 100% -> env C, flagged Low confidence). 5 recorded Not Classified on a stated consensus - Solvent Orange 60 (2229/2274), CI Acid Blue 145 (5/5), Tripropylene Glycol Butyl Ether (no GHS section in PubChem), Diethylene Glycol (H302 100% of 38 notifications; acute oral is not a graded dimension), and 8 recorded unclassified with explicit sourcing notes because they are UVCB/petroleum streams, minerals, materials or withheld trade-secret names with no PubChem CID (Petroleum Distillates Hydrotreated Light, Aliphatic Ether Alcohol, Glycol Ether, Polyester Sheet, Dialkylester Dimethyl Ammonium Methosulfate, Fatty Acids C16-18, Bentonite, Ethoxylated C8-18 Alkylamines, Turpentine) - never an invented grade. METHOD FINDING (recorded, not silently worked around): PubChem PUG View returns GHS classifications grouped by ECHA C&L notification group, and each group carries its own denominator. tools/grade_batch.py flattens all groups into one h_statements list, so a >=40% figure from a 2-notification fringe group is indistinguishable from a 19-notification consensus. Methenamine is the live example: its dominant group (19 notifications) carries H228+H317, while a separate 2-notification group carries H302/H314/H334/H351 at '100%' - within-group, not global. Those fringe codes were NOT graded. Grades in this run were taken from the dominant group with the denominator stated in each note. Regulatory: added a Nonoxynol entry (EU REACH Annex XVII entry 46 restricts NP/NPE at >=0.1% in domestic cleaning; US has no consumer-cleaner restriction) - The Works Toilet Bowl Cleaner discloses nonoxynol on a mainstream US product, which is the EU/US gap this section exists to show. Check attempted and REJECTED: Diethylene Glycol is not asserted as an EU harmonised Repr. 1B - the search result that suggested it was mixing in the borate row (same H360FD / 5.5% SCL), and the manufacturer SDSs found say DEG is not classified for reproductive or repeated-exposure toxicity. No reg entry filed.

Gather: 4 popular US cleaning products with public disclosures - Purex Free & Clear Liquid Laundry Detergent (Henkel/Purex public disclosure), Spray 'n Wash Laundry Stain Remover (Reckitt rbnainfo.com SmartLabel + SDS), Ivory Concentrated Dishwashing Liquid Classic Scent (P&G SmartLabel), fantastik Disinfectant Multi-Purpose Cleaner Fresh Scent (SC Johnson 'What's Inside'). 7 new ingredients: calcium chloride, potassium chloride, diisopropanolamine, sodium polyacrylate, fluorescent brightener 28, protease enzyme, PEI-14 PEG-24/PPG-16 copolymer. 3 graded from PubChem/ECHA C&L via tools/ghs_lookup.py with consensus percentages cited (calcium chloride H319 99.7% -> derm C; diisopropanolamine H318 51.2% -> derm D; fluorescent brightener 28 268/274 not-classified); 1 not-classified on consensus (potassium chloride 825/875); 3 recorded unclassified/extrapolated with explicit sourcing notes because they are UVCB/polymers or generic class terms with no PubChem CID (sodium polyacrylate, PEI-14 copolymer, protease enzyme) - never an invented grade. Headline findings: (1) Spray 'n Wash discloses sodium tetraborate decahydrate (borax) as a sequestering agent - the same substance EU CLP classifies Reproductive toxicant 1B (H360FD) and restricts for consumer supply, still routine in a mainstream US stain remover. (2) Purex Free & Clear, marketed for sensitive skin as dye- and perfume-free, still contains methylisothiazolinone (a potent contact allergen) and sodium laureth sulfate. (3) fantastik's fragrance disclosure includes butylphenyl methylpropional (Lilial), an EU-banned CMR fragrance, plus hexyl cinnamal. 149 products, 219 ingredients.

Gather: 4 popular US cleaning products with public disclosures — Persil ProClean Liquid Laundry Detergent Intense Fresh (Henkel SmartLabel, verified 16-Jan-2025), Clorox Clean-Up All Purpose Cleaner with Bleach Original (Clorox SmartLabel updated 11/19/2024 + SDS EPA Reg. 5813-21), Spic and Span All-Purpose Disinfecting Spray and Glass Cleaner (Church & Dwight SDS + retail disclosure), Downy Ultra Free & Gentle Liquid Fabric Conditioner (P&G SmartLabel updated 2024-11-04). 20 new ingredients. 13 graded from PubChem/ECHA C&L via tools/ghs_lookup.py, each with its consensus percentages cited and any sub-40% codes noted: laureth-12, sodium metaborate, tetrasodium iminodisuccinate, disodium distyrylbiphenyl disulfonate, myristamine oxide, sodium chlorate, benzophenone, sodium orthosilicate, isopropanolamine, tartaric acid, formic acid, pentasodium pentetate, cellulase enzyme. 7 recorded unclassified/extrapolated with explicit sourcing notes because they are UVCB/polymers with no PubChem CID (fatty acid sodium soaps, polyethyleneimine alkoxylate, the acrylate/styrene copolymer, the polyoxyalkylene chromophore, mannanase enzyme, DEEDMAC, polyquaternium-33) — never an invented grade. Headline findings: (1) benzophenone, prohibited in EU cosmetics (Annex II, Entry 1703) and IARC 2B, is disclosed on the US label of a mainstream bleach spray cleaner — added as a reclassified entry plus a new reg entry (EU banned / US flagged). (2) sodium metaborate, the borate enzyme stabilizer in Persil, carries the same EU CLP Reproductive toxicant 1B (H360FD) classification as borax — added as a reclassified entry plus a reg entry (EU restricted / US allowed). (3) sodium chlorate on the Clorox Clean-Up label is not an added ingredient — it forms as the hypochlorite decays in storage (3 NaOCl -> NaClO3 + 2 NaCl), documented in the OxyChem hypochlorite handbook. (4) Downy Free & Gentle is marketed perfume-free yet still discloses a 'Fragrance Ingredient'. Verification note: the PubChem name lookup for 'Protease' silently returned Bacillomycin (CID 3086051) — a different compound — so it was discarded and the disclosure recorded under the existing 'Subtilisin' entry instead. Validator: pending. Products 141 -> 145, ingredient keys 192 -> 212.

Gather: 4 popular US cleaning products with public disclosures — Clorox Disinfecting Wipes Fresh Scent (Clorox SmartLabel, updated 4/8/2025), OxiClean Versatile Stain Remover (Church & Dwight SDS), Woolite Delicates Laundry Detergent (Reckitt SmartLabel), Mr. Clean Magic Eraser (P&G SDS composition section). 15 new ingredients. 7 graded from PubChem/ECHA C&L via tools/ghs_lookup.py (hexoxyethanol, triethanolamine, BHT, butylphenyl methylpropional, hexyl salicylate, isoeugenol, eugenol), each with its consensus percentages cited and any sub-40% codes noted. 8 recorded unclassified/extrapolated with explicit sourcing notes because they are UVCB/polymers with no PubChem CID (sodium polycarboxylate, the melamine-formaldehyde copolymer, the two BAC-type quats, TEA cocoate, C10-16 pareth, C12-14 alcohols ethoxylated propoxylated, sodium C10-16 alkylbenzenesulfonate) — never an invented grade. Headline finding: butylphenyl methylpropional (Lilial), a CMR 1B fragrance banned in EU cosmetics since 2022, is still disclosed in a US detergent — added as a reclassified entry plus a new reg entry (EU banned / US allowed) noting the SCCS record that the cosmetics ban does not reach household cleaners. Validator: 0 issues. 141 products, 192 ingredients.

Root-cause fix for the duplicate bug that had been hand-fixed five times: the grow lane's dedupe index was keyed raw (.strip().lower()) while its lookup used norm() (punctuation collapsed), so every seed product whose name or brand contains punctuation (P&G, Free & Clear, Multi-Surface) silently re-added itself each run — which is exactly why Clorox Disinfecting Bleach, the one seed with no punctuation, never duplicated. Index normalized in bulk_ingest.py and a permanent `chem_maintain.py --dedupe --fix` guard wired into chem_cron.sh, so duplicates can no longer survive a run. Removed 4 duplicates (137->133). Schema fixes: 3 invalid enum values closed — Bac-Out impact 'sens'->'allerg', and the non-canonical grade dim 'allerg' on Linalool/Geraniol merged into derm:D per the house H317 rule (matching Citral/Limonene/Fragrance). Gather: 4 popular US products with public disclosures — Resolve Heavy Traffic Foam Carpet Cleaner (Reckitt SmartLabel), Krud Kutter Original Cleaner & Degreaser (Rust-Oleum SDS), Weiman Stainless Steel Cleaner & Polish (Weiman ingredient list), LA's Totally Awesome All-Purpose Cleaner (manufacturer MSDS + retail composition — flagged as weaker sourcing, not presented as equivalent). 12 new ingredients, each graded from PubChem/ECHA C&L via tools/ghs_lookup.py where a CID exists, or recorded unclassified with an explicit note where it does not (UVCB/polymer) rather than guessing a grade. Added CMIT regulatory entry: EU leave-on cosmetics ban since 2016, no equivalent US federal restriction in cleaning products. Validator: 0 issues. 137 products, 177 ingredients.
